newsitem.title: USA: Chase Telecom says to raise cash "sooner vs later".
newsitem.headline: Chase Telecom says to raise cash "sooner vs later".

text.p: Chase Telecommunications Inc on Tuesday said it is still optimistic about raising funds for its fledgling personal communications services (PCS) system following a rebuff from high-yield investors last week.

"We're optimistic about having another financing event in the near-term," said Mary Bogue, vice president of finance at Chase Telecommunications, adding that it will be "sooner versus later -- timing is critical for everybody."

A new capital-raising effort could take one of "numerous" forms, including another possible foray into the debt markets or an equity offering, Bogue said. With the money, Bogue said the company can still launch its PCS service in the second quarter of 1998 as planned.

Chase's planned $160 million junk bond deal was indefinitely postponed last week due to "difficulties in raising money for developmental PCS," according to a source close to the deal. The deal went through one restructuring -- it was transformed from a zero coupon to a prefunded structure -- before dropping from the calendar.

Chase, which would provide services primarily in Tennessee, was a winner of "C block" PCS licenses in the Federal Communications Commission's auction last year. The C block auction gave preference to entrepreneurial companies such as NextWave Telecom Inc and Pocket Communications Inc, both of which have also withdrawn high-yield offerings.
Financing from large PCS players Qualcomm Inc and PrimeCo Personal Communications are still in the works, Bogue said.

PrimeCo, a joint venture between AirTouch Communications Inc and several regional Bell telephone companies, stands to acquire a 13-percent stake in Chase in return for providing various services and through the conversion of a $2 million outstanding loan.

Qualcomm has agreed to provide Chase with $25 million in notes in exchange for warrants to purchase 10 percent of the company's stock. Qualcomm is also slated to provide $119 million of vendor financing to Chase following the transaction.
AirTouch and Qualcomm did not immediately return phone calls.
